mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines ductility of a metal?

options.A: Ability to be drawn into wires
options.B: Ability to be hammered into sheets

mcqs.answer: Ability to be drawn into wires
mcqs.explanation: Ductility is the property that allows a metal to be stretched into a thin wire without breaking. Option B describes malleability, C describes conductivity, and D describes lustre. Hence, option A is correct.

mcqs.question: If a wire needs to transmit electricity with minimum loss, which metal would be most suitable?
mcqs.explanation: Copper has a very high electrical conductivity, second only to silver, making it the preferred material for electrical wiring. Iron, lead, and zinc have considerably lower conductivities, so they would cause higher energy loss.

mcqs.question: Which of the following metals produces a clear ringing sound when struck, illustrating sonority?
mcqs.explanation: Sonority refers to the ability of a metal to emit a clear, resonant sound when struck. Aluminum is known for its good sonorous quality, whereas lead and tin produce dull sounds and mercury is liquid at room temperature, so it cannot be struck.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify exceptions to common metallic properties
mcqs.question: A student observes that a certain metal is liquid at room temperature, does not exhibit typical metallic luster, and cannot be hammered into sheets. Which metal is this?
mcqs.explanation: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature, lacks the usual metallic lustre, and cannot be hammered. Iron, copper, and aluminum are solid, lustrous, and malleable, so they do not fit the description.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about lustre is incorrect?

options.A: Metals have a characteristic shiny appearance called metallic lustre.
options.B: All objects that appear shiny are metals.
options.C: Lustre is due to reflection of light from the surface.
options.D: Non-metals can also be polished to appear lustrous.

mcqs.answer: All objects that appear shiny are metals.
mcqs.explanation: While metals typically exhibit metallic lustre, many non‑metallic substances (e.g., glass, polished plastic) can also appear shiny. Therefore, statement B is the misconception.

mcqs.question: Malleability of metals is primarily due to which of the following reasons?

options.A: Presence of non‑directional metallic bonds allowing layers to slide
options.C: Presence of free electrons causing electrical conductivity
options.D: Strong ionic bonds between metal atoms

mcqs.answer: Presence of non‑directional metallic bonds allowing layers to slide
mcqs.explanation: Malleability arises because metallic bonds are non‑directional; when a force is applied, whole layers of atoms can shift without breaking the bond network. High melting point, conductivity, and ionic bonds are unrelated to malleability.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly compares a ductile metal with a brittle metal in terms of their behavior under tensile stress?

options.A: Copper can be drawn into wires, while cast iron breaks into fragments.
options.B: Cast iron can be drawn into wires, while copper breaks into fragments.
options.C: Both copper and cast iron can be drawn into wires.
options.D: Both copper and cast iron break into fragments.

mcqs.answer: Copper can be drawn into wires, while cast iron breaks into fragments.
mcqs.explanation: Copper is a classic ductile metal; it can be stretched into thin wires. Cast iron is brittle; under tensile stress it fractures rather than deforming. Options B, C, and D contradict these well‑known behaviors.

mcqs.question: Among the following metals, which one has the highest electrical conductivity?
mcqs.explanation: Silver possesses the greatest electrical conductivity of all metals, a fact frequently tested in competitive exams. Copper is the second best, while gold and aluminum have lower conductivities.
